explanation: Because ParentID is nullable, a null foreign key is allowed when the relationship is optional. Values 5, 9, and 11 do not exist in Parent, so they would violate referential integrity.

options.text: INSERT INTO Child (ChildID, ParentID) VALUES (21, NULL);

prompt: A MySQL database has these tables: Parent(ParentID PRIMARY KEY) and Child(ChildID PRIMARY KEY, ParentID INT NULL, FOREIGN KEY (ParentID) REFERENCES Parent(ParentID)). Which insert is allowed by referential integrity? Assume Parent currently contains ParentID values 3 and 8.
reviewConcept: An optional foreign key may be null; otherwise it must match a parent key.
